What you could spend today without taking it from any envelope: the money in Unassigned minus what the envelopes have gone below zero.
The line shows how it moves day by day until the end of the period as due dates are paid and expected income comes in; dashed is the future.
“Projected” is where it will end. The figure beside it is what explains the difference: commitments the envelopes cannot cover, contributions to other groups or expected income.
The money in your accounts that is not in any envelope yet (Unassigned). Give it a job by assigning it to envelopes.
The rows show how it is made: what is in your accounts, minus the payments of this period, what is set aside for later and the rest of the envelopes.
Below zero means the envelopes hold more than your accounts have: move money out of an envelope or wait for the income that covers it.
The sum of the balances of every live account of the group, as the database computes it.
Accounts outside the envelopes (savings, investments) count here but their money is not distributed into envelopes.
What the commitments will bring in and take out of this account until the end of the period, overdue ones included, and the balance it will end with.
If it goes below zero on the way, the warning says by how much and on which day, so you can move money in before.
How the envelope\'s period went: what it brought from the last period, what was assigned to it, what was spent from it and what is left.
What is left is carried to the next period.
The envelope\'s balance minus what pending commitments will still take from it until the end of the period (or the day you choose).
When the commitments need more than the envelope has, the difference will have to come from elsewhere.
Choose a filter (an account, an envelope, dates, a tag…) to see how much came in and went out.
